title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
summary_en: Foundational issue-to-pull-request benchmark construction pipeline, connecting a repository snapshot, a natural-language issue, a reference patch, and executable tests.

title: Introducing SWE-bench Verified
summary_en: Human-screened SWE-bench subset and public annotation rubric, useful as a baseline for checking whether issue descriptions and hidden tests define a fair task.

title: Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym
summary_en: Builds executable training tasks from real GitHub issues, then uses the resulting interactions to train agents and trajectory verifiers.

title: R2E-Gym: Procedural Environments and Hybrid Verifiers for Scaling Open-Weights SWE Agents
summary_en: Constructs executable training tasks from commits with synthesized tests and issue descriptions; uses test execution and learned scoring models to rank candidate repairs.

title: SWE-smith: Scaling Data for Software Engineering Agents
summary_en: Creates an environment first, then injects synthetic bugs into existing repositories and generates issue descriptions for agent training.

title: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
summary_en: Combines automated executable-task collection with learned quality assessment and continuously refreshed evaluation tasks.

title: SWE-bench Goes Live!
summary_en: Introduces SWE-bench-Live and RepoLaunch to collect recent real issues and automate their execution environments.

title: SWE-Factory: Your Automated Factory for Issue Resolution Training Data and Evaluation Benchmarks
summary_en: Automates issue collection and environment setup, then checks whether tests fail before a reference fix and pass afterward.

title: SWE-Bench Pro: Can AI Agents Solve Long-Horizon Software Engineering Tasks?
summary_en: Constructs harder repository tasks with human-augmented requirements, explicit interfaces, reviewed tests, and containerized environments.

title: Immersion in the GitHub Universe: Scaling Coding Agents to Mastery
summary_en: ScaleSWE coordinates agents for Docker setup, test generation, and problem-statement synthesis from GitHub pull requests.

title: SWE-rebench V2: Language-Agnostic SWE Task Collection at Scale
summary_en: Extends automated collection across languages, adding setup synthesis, issue-clarity filtering, and diagnostic metadata about task quality.

title: SWE-World: Building Software Engineering Agents in Docker-Free Environments
summary_en: Replaces expensive repository execution with learned transition and reward models while preserving deterministic file operations.

title: SWE-Bench+: Enhanced Coding Benchmark for LLMs
summary_en: Audits SWE-bench patches that passed existing tests and distinguishes exposed solutions, incorrect or incomplete fixes, and legitimate alternatives to the reference patch.

title: Are "Solved Issues" in SWE-bench Really Solved Correctly? An Empirical Study
summary_en: Studies test-passing SWE-bench Verified patches using broader developer tests and PatchDiff, which generates tests exposing behavioral differences between an agent patch and the reference fix.

title: UTBoost: Rigorous Evaluation of Coding Agents on SWE-Bench
summary_en: Augments SWE-bench tests to expose previously accepted incorrect patches and separately fixes evaluation-log parsing errors that can corrupt pass/fail annotations.
affiliation: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

title: SPICE: An Automated SWE-Bench Labeling Pipeline for Issue Clarity, Test Coverage, and Effort Estimation
summary_en: Automates SWE-bench-style dataset review with separate issue-clarity and test-adequacy assessments, following the SWE-bench Verified annotation rubric.

title: Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding capabilities
summary_en: OpenAI documents residual test/specification defects in SWE-bench Verified and evidence that frontier models can recall some benchmark solutions.

title: Separating signal from noise in coding evaluations
summary_en: Audits SWE-Bench Pro through automated triage, investigator agents with repository/environment access, and independent software-engineer review.

title: Can LLMs Detect Benchmark Defects? A Meta-Benchmark from Benchmark Updates
summary_en: Task Verification Bench evaluates whether agents can identify benchmark defects, using SWE-bench human annotations and Terminal-Bench repair histories as reference evidence.

title: Who Guards the Benchmarks? Automated Auditing of LLM Agent Benchmarks
summary_en: BenchGuard cross-checks instructions, reference programs, evaluation scripts and environment configurations, evaluated primarily on scientific agent tasks.

title: Automated Benchmark Auditing for AI Agents and Large Language Models
summary_en: Organizes instructions, environment files and grading code for evidence-linked audits using task materials or recorded agent runs, including coding benchmarks.

title: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks with BenchJack
summary_en: Uses coding agents to find ways of receiving credit without completing a task, then repairs exposed grading weaknesses, including SWE-bench cases.

title: SWE-Bench Pro Verified: A Reliable Benchmark for Software Engineering Agents
summary_en: Repairs SWE-Bench Pro through two tracks: reducing accessible solution/evaluation leakage and refining confirmed task-description or test defects.
affiliation: East China Normal University; Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

title: Benchmarking Reward Hack Detection in Code Environments via Contrastive Analysis
scope: code-environment trajectories; adjacent to task-package audits
summary_en: Introduces TRACE, a human-checked synthetic trajectory benchmark for evaluating reward-hack detectors in code environments; contrasts isolated classification with comparison across trajectories.

title: Automated Transcript Analysis for Detecting Flaws in Agentic Benchmarks
summary_en: Develops transcript scanners for ground-truth access, tool failures, guessing and answer-format ambiguity; includes SWE-bench Verified, KernelBench and Terminal-Bench cases.

title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
summary_en: EvalPlus augments code-generation benchmarks with automatically generated test inputs to expose incorrect programs that small original test suites accept.

title: Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals
summary_en: Measures how sandbox resource allocation changes coding-evaluation reliability and scores.

title: Terminal-Bench Science: task review automation and quality rubric
scope: terminal/scientific workflows; adjacent to repository repair
summary_en: Combines static checks, rubric review, reference-solution runs and no-op runs in a task contribution workflow.

title: Continuous Benchmarks
summary_en: Treats benchmarks as maintained software, with production feedback informing quality checks and versioned changes.

title: Terminal-Bench 4.0: resource calibration and task fixes
summary_en: Documents task fixes, resource calibration and version rules for rerunning or regrading evaluations.

title: Automated Benchmark Generation for Repository-Level Coding Tasks
summary_en: SetUpAgent turns real issue-linked pull requests into executable repository tasks by reconstructing environments and checking the reference fix against tests. Its pipeline is useful for studying setup reliability and test-level filtering during benchmark construction.

title: Training Versatile Coding Agents in Synthetic Environments
summary_en: SWE-Playground creates synthetic repository environments and tasks for coding-agent training, with separate generation and execution checks for task tests and implementations. Its issue-adaptation experiments also connect synthetic tasks to real repository issues.

title: Multi-SWE-bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Issue Resolving
summary_en: Multi-SWE-bench extends issue-resolution evaluation across languages and documents a construction pipeline combining runnable repository environments, patch/test execution, and human annotation. The final NeurIPS dataset contains 2,132 tasks, including the reused 500-task SWE-bench Verified subset and additional multilingual instances.

title: Multi-SWT-Bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Reproduction Test Generation
summary_en: Multi-SWT-Bench adapts multilingual repository issues into a benchmark for generating tests that reproduce the reported bug. It filters tasks by executing developer-written tests against buggy and fixed repository states.

title: Synthesizing Software Engineering Data in a Test-Driven Manner
scope: repository-level synthetic training and evaluation data
summary_en: SWE-Flow synthesizes repository-level software tasks from existing tests and their runtime dependencies. It filters unusable tests and uses a runtime dependency graph to derive code-generation tasks from tested behavior.
affiliation: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: SWT-Bench: Testing and Validating Real-World Bug-Fixes with Code Agents
summary_en: SWT-Bench evaluates whether agents can write tests that reproduce real repository bugs and validate fixes. Its construction filters issue/PR cases using execution of the reference fix and generated or collected reproduction tests.

title: MCTS-Refined CoT: High-Quality Fine-Tuning Data for LLM-Based Repository Issue Resolution
summary_en: MCTS-Refined CoT filters and refines repository-issue reasoning traces using stepwise gold-aligned checks for localization and patching. It is relevant to trajectory quality for fine-tuning, rather than a standalone task benchmark audit.

title: On Data Engineering for Scaling LLM Terminal Capabilities
scope: terminal tasks, including repository-adjacent software engineering
summary_en: This work describes engineering a large terminal-agent training corpus from seed tasks and synthetic tasks, with executable environments, test expectations, and dataset-level filtering. It is broader than repository issue resolution but includes concrete task and trajectory quality controls.

title: SWE-bench Multimodal: Do AI Systems Generalize to Visual Software Domains?
summary_en: SWE-bench Multimodal extends issue-resolution tasks to software whose behavior is assessed through visual interfaces. The official benchmark page documents the September 2026 Multimodal V2 update with 480 tasks, reproducible selection, removal of known flaky or ungradeable tests, and environment/grading maintenance.

title: PAIChecker: Uncovering and Checking PR-Issue Misalignment in SWE-Bench-Like Benchmarks
summary_en: PAIChecker treats mismatches between a GitHub issue and its linked pull request as a construction defect in SWE-bench-like datasets. It proposes a multi-agent checker that combines issue/PR evidence with code-level validation.
affiliation: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

title: Coding Agents as Test-Suite Auditors: Finding What Official Suites Miss While Approaching What They Catch
scope: Competitive-programming online-judge tasks; adjacent to repository-level software-engineering benchmarks
summary_en: This work uses coding agents to generate adversarial tests that check whether official online-judge suites accept buggy submissions. A multi-step certification process independently checks expected outputs and input legality, making the discovered verifier gaps auditable.

title: SWE-Mutation: Can LLMs Generate Reliable Test Suites in Software Engineering?
scope: Software-engineering task test suites and generated-test evaluation
summary_en: SWE-Mutation benchmarks the discriminative power of test suites by checking whether semantically meaningful code mutants can still pass. It also studies how an agentic mutation process changes the difficulty of evaluating test-generation systems.
affiliation: University of Science and Technology of China

title: Does SWE-Bench-Verified Test Agent Ability or Model Memory?
scope: Repository-level issue localization on SWE-bench Verified and comparison datasets
summary_en: This study probes possible benchmark exposure by asking two Claude models to localize edited files from issue text with deliberately limited context. The authors report much higher localization on SWE-bench Verified than on BeetleBox and SWE-rebench, which is consistent with possible task familiarity but does not establish training-set contamination.

title: Saving SWE-Bench: A Benchmark Mutation Approach for Realistic Agent Evaluation
scope: Repository-level issue-prompt realism and agent evaluation protocol
summary_en: This work rewrites formal GitHub issues into user-style prompts derived from coding-assistant interaction patterns, then compares agent performance on the original and mutated task descriptions. It measures how task presentation can change reported bug-fixing performance, rather than auditing hidden-test correctness.

title: A Determinacy Audit of SWE-bench Pro
scope: Public SWE-bench Pro task specifications and official verifiers
summary_en: This independent report audits all 728 public SWE-bench Pro tasks for whether the materials given to a solver determine the behavior checked by hidden tests. It reports a 15.0% conservative underdetermination floor, including a mechanically supported subset, and three reference patches that fail the official verifier.

title: Probe to Generate: Program Variant-Guided Test Augmentation for Repository-Level Repair Benchmarks
scope: Repository-level repair benchmark regression tests; evaluation on SWE-bench Verified
summary_en: PROBE uses variants of a reference repair to identify potential gaps in a benchmark's tests. It generates additional tests that distinguish reference repairs from surviving variants, then checks their robustness under behavior-preserving transformations.
